required_patterns.route-definitions: Use Express Router. Routes are defined in the `src/routes/` directory.

architectural_constraints.route-mounting: All routers must be mounted in `src/server.ts` under the `/api/v1/...` path structure.

required_patterns.async-error-handling: Wrap all asynchronous route handlers in `asyncHandler` (from `src/utils/asyncHandler.ts`) to automatically pass errors to Express.

architectural_constraints.separation-of-concerns: Handlers must only extract `req` data, invoke `services`, and format `res` output. No complex business logic.

required_patterns.business-logic: Encapsulate core business logic, database queries, and third-party API interactions (e.g., Cloudinary) in `src/services/`.

architectural_constraints.http-agnostic: Services must not directly interact with Express `req` or `res` objects. They should throw custom `AppError` on failure.

required_patterns.auth: Use `authenticate` and `authorize` middleware to protect secured routes.
required_patterns.validation: Use `validateBody` middleware with Zod schemas (imported from shared package) to validate request payloads.

architectural_constraints.pre-handler-execution: Middleware must be chained in route definitions before the final handler executes.

required_patterns.mongodb-models: Import and use Mongoose models (like `Product`) and connection utilities directly from the workspace package `@jhaz-imprints/catalog-db`.

architectural_constraints.no-prisma: This microservice uses MongoDB via Mongoose. Prisma (which is used elsewhere in the monorepo) is strictly forbidden here.

required_patterns.custom-errors: Use the custom `AppError` class (from `src/errors/AppError.ts`) to throw operational errors with specific HTTP status codes.

architectural_constraints.global-handling: Errors must bubble up to the global Express error handler rather than being manually caught and sent as responses in every function.
